subject: anatomy
title: Small Intestine: Jejunum versus Ileum, Vascular Arcades, and Appendix

steps.tx: The mesenteric small intestine measures approximately six meters in length, extending from the duodenojejunal flexure to the ileocaecal valve. The proximal two-fifths (2.5 meters) constitutes the **jejunum**, situated predominantly in the left upper quadrant, while the distal three-fifths (3.5 meters) forms the ileum in the right lower quadrant.
steps.say: The small intestine measures six meters from the duodenojejunal flexure to the ileocaecal valve. The proximal two-fifths is the jejunum in the left upper quadrant, while the distal three-fifths forms the ileum.

vis.caption: Topographical quadrants distinguishing jejunal coils in LUQ from ileal loops in RLQ. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Differentiating jejunum from ileum is an essential surgical skill during emergency bowel resection. The jejunum possesses a thicker, more muscular and hypervascular wall, a wider lumen, and prominent circular mucosal folds called **plicae circulares** (valvulae conniventes), which are tall, closely packed, and readily palpable.
steps.say: Distinguishing jejunum from ileum is vital during laparotomy. The jejunum has a thicker, redder wall, wider lumen, and prominent circular plicae circulares that are easily felt through the wall.

left.title: Jejunum Characteristics
points: Location: left upper quadrant and umbilical
Wall: thick, heavy, hyperemic, and fleshy
Mucosa: prominent, closely packed plicae circulares

right.title: Ileum Characteristics
points: Location: right lower quadrant and pelvis
Wall: thin, light, pale, and collapsible
Mucosa: sparse plicae; prominent Peyer patches

steps.tx: The architecture of the mesenteric vasculature provides the most definitive distinction between small bowel loops. In the jejunal mesentery, the branches of the superior mesenteric artery form only one or two simple **arterial arcades**, giving rise to long, straight, parallel terminal vessels termed vasa recta.
steps.say: Mesenteric vascular patterns offer the most reliable surgical distinction. The jejunal mesentery features only one or two simple arterial arcades giving off long, straight vasa recta.

left.title: Jejunal Mesenteric Pattern
points: Vasa recta are long, straight, and distinct
Mesenteric fat is sparse near the bowel wall

right.title: Ileal Mesenteric Pattern
points: Vasa recta are short, narrow, and crowded
Mesenteric fat extends completely onto bowel serosa

steps.tx: In contrast, the ileal mesentery exhibits three, four, or five complex tiers of short cascading arterial arcades with very short **vasa recta**. Furthermore, mesenteric fat encroaches completely onto the antimesenteric border of the ileum, obliterating the translucent peritoneal windows seen in the jejunum.
steps.say: In contrast, the ileal mesentery contains multiple tiers of crowded arcades with very short vasa recta. Fat encroaches completely onto the ileal wall, leaving no translucent windows.

rows: Held up against operating room lights

steps.tx: Aggregations of unencapsulated subepithelial lymphoid follicles termed **Peyer patches** predominate in the antimesenteric mucosa of the terminal ileum. Serving as antigen-sampling centers for mucosal IgA production, they represent the primary site of infection in typhoid fever, where Salmonella Typhi causes mucosal ulceration and bowel perforation.
steps.say: Peyer patches are aggregated lymphoid follicles along the antimesenteric border of the terminal ileum. They serve as mucosal immune centers and are the primary site of ulceration and perforation in typhoid fever.

steps.tx: The junction in this picture is a one way door with an immune outpost beside it. At the **ileocaecal junction**, ileal contents enter the caecum while reflux is resisted, and the nearby appendix and Peyer patches sample what passes. Barium studies and endoscopists use this landmark constantly, because reaching it proves a complete colonoscopy. Inflammation centred here narrows the differential quickly toward Crohn disease, tuberculosis, typhoid and malignancy rather than ordinary colitis.
steps.say: The ileocaecal junction admits ileal contents into the caecum and landmarks a complete colonoscopy. Disease centred here suggests Crohn disease, tuberculosis, typhoid or tumour.

vis.alt: Anatomical diagram of the ileocaecal junction, terminal ileum entering the caecum beside the appendix opening.
vis.caption: Terminal ileum is shown entering the caecum at the ileocaecal junction, with the appendix opening below. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: The terminal ileum enters the large intestine at the **ileocaecal junction**, guarded by the ileocaecal valve (valvula coli) consisting of upper and lower horizontal lips. The valve prevents retrograde reflux of fecal contents from the bacteria-dense caecum into the relatively sterile ileum.
steps.say: The terminal ileum empties into the caecum at the ileocaecal valve. Its two horizontal lips prevent retrograde reflux of bacteria-laden colonic contents into the sterile small intestine.

steps.tx: The vermiform appendix arises from the posteromedial wall of the caecum approximately two centimetres below the ileocaecal junction, where the three longitudinal taeniae coli converge. The anatomical position of the appendiceal tip varies widely, with the **retrocaecal position** being the most frequent (65%), followed by the pelvic position (30%).
steps.say: The vermiform appendix arises from the posteromedial caecum where the three taeniae coli unite. The retrocaecal position is the most common at sixty-five percent, followed by the pelvic position at thirty percent.

rows: Silent peritonitis; positive psoas stretch sign
Diarrhea, dysuria, rectal tenderness on PR

steps.tx: Surface projection of the base of the appendix corresponds to **McBurney point**, located at the junction of the lateral third and medial two-thirds of a line drawn from the anterior superior iliac spine to the umbilicus. Maximum tenderness at McBurney point reflects somatic peritoneal irritation in acute appendicitis.
steps.say: The base of the appendix lies at McBurney point, one-third of the way along the line from the right ASIS to the umbilicus. Sharp localized tenderness here indicates acute appendicitis.
